source.title: Anti-correlated noise in epoch-based stochastic gradient descent: implications for weight variances in flat directions

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares generalization performance under with-replacement and without-replacement SGD and measures weight variance across Hessian directions. These are different conditions and measurements from the listed versions, so the findings fit none of them.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites prior work on flat minima, gradient noise, and generalization; those cited results are not extracted as this study's own findings. The 62% escaping-efficiency reduction is a theoretical prediction, not a measured test-performance result.
record.test_reason: The study tests sampling with versus without replacement and predictions about SGD fluctuations, but none of V1–V8. Its curvature and weight-variance measurements do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap ranking. Appendix G.5 varies batch size but reports fluctuation statistics, without held-out performance comparisons needed for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive and empirically validate noise anti-correlations and reduced weight variance in flatter Hessian directions, and report higher maximum test accuracy without replacement. Their proposed connection through convergence to flatter minima remains an interpretation; they explicitly leave establishing that connection to future research.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD with momentum and epoch-based without-replacement sampling; compares against sampling with replacement. It does not test the interventions or measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight-variance behavior differs by Hessian eigenvalue relative to λcross; small-curvature directions show slight departures from the predicted proportionality. Sampling with replacement removes the observed noise anti-correlations and changes the variance and correlation-time behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: LeNet on CIFAR-10 achieved mean maximum test accuracy of 69.8% without replacement versus 69.0% with replacement across 20 seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sampling without replacement can improve maximum test accuracy under this LeNet training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Under sampling without replacement, weight variance is approximately constant above a curvature crossover and proportional to curvature below it, with deviations in the flattest measured directions; ResNet-20 also agrees with the fluctuation theory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-based SGD noise anti-correlations suppress stationary weight fluctuations in low-curvature directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Using LeNet's 5,000 largest Hessian eigenvalues, the theoretical model predicts a 62% reduction in stationary escaping efficiency without replacement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise anti-correlations can reduce model-predicted loss fluctuations near a minimum.

record.problems: The main LeNet analysis uses one seed and a restricted subspace of the 5,000 largest Hessian eigenvectors; the authors report additional seeds and hyperparameters qualitatively in an appendix. The test-accuracy comparison reports 20 seeds and a stated ± value, but the text does not define that uncertainty statistic. The escaping-efficiency reduction is predicted from a model, not measured directly.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Figures G5 and G6 describe sampling and variance comparisons mainly visually; the text does not give separate numeric values suitable for additional rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps across comparably trained networks and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measurements fit no version; this does not dispute the reported findings. The main LeNet recipe includes L2 regularization with coefficient 0.005, momentum 0.9, batch size 50, and 300 training epochs.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out chance-accuracy comparison.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measure or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: LeNet
rows.stage_stated: trained 300 epochs; analysis over 20 additional epochs
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy after training with examples sampled without replacement versus with replacement.

conditions.value: maximum test accuracy computed after each epoch

rows.value: 69.8% on average; 0.8% ± 0.2% higher than with replacement
rows.note: The paper attributes the improvement to anti-correlations as a proposed interpretation; this comparison does not test any listed version.
rows.check: The reported comparison is accurate but measures a sampling intervention outside all listed versions. The improvement is 0.8 ± 0.2 percentage points in maximum test accuracy across epochs, averaged over 20 seeds, rather than final-epoch accuracy. The uncertainty statistic is undefined.

rows.subject: LeNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured weight variance along the 5,000 largest Hessian eigenvectors against Hessian eigenvalues.
rows.baseline: Constant weight variance prediction from prior literature
rows.value: Variance follows different regimes: approximately constant above λcross and proportional to λi below λcross; slight deviations in the very lowest-curvature directions
rows.note: The paper describes its theoretical predictions as closely followed, with slight low-curvature deviations; this does not measure the sharpness metric specified by V7.
rows.check: Weight variance along Hessian directions does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or its association with generalization gaps. The small deviations from the paper's variance theory cannot establish a partial effect for any listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained 300 epochs; analysis in subspace of 400 largest Hessian eigenvalues
rows.operation_detail: Measured weight and velocity variances and correlation times across Hessian directions.
rows.measure: Weight variance and correlation time by Hessian eigenvalue
rows.value: Numerical observations show good agreement with the theory predictions
rows.note: The paper reports 100% training accuracy and 76% test accuracy for this setup, but does not compare these accuracies against another condition.
rows.check: Agreement between fluctuation theory and ResNet-20 measurements does not test any listed version. The accompanying 100% training and 76% test accuracies provide neither the required architectural comparison nor a sharpness–gap comparison.

rows.subject: LeNet
rows.operation_detail: Estimated reduction in escaping efficiency using the 5,000 largest Hessian eigenvalues and the paper's model.
rows.value: 62% reduction in escaping efficiency for the case without replacement
rows.note: This is a model-based prediction about escaping efficiency, not a measured generalization result.
rows.check: The 62% reduction is a model prediction using measured Hessian eigenvalues, not an observed escape rate or generalization effect. Retain only as a theoretical finding, not an empirical behavior row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
